title: tsfm-anomaly-detection: experimental harness, results and analysis for "When Do Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models Pay Off for Anomaly Detection?"

creators.name: Cai, Siyu
creators.affiliation: School of Computing and Artificial Intelligence, Southwest Jiaotong University

description:
The experimental harness, merged result records and analysis code behind a negative result: eight zero-shot configurations of four pretrained time-series foundation models, compared against four classical detectors on 360 series from four public benchmarks (UCR Anomaly Archive 2021, SMD, SMAP/MSL, PSM), for 5504 result records and a separately measured cost profile. The protocol defines three baseline tiers; the default and tuned tiers were run and the oracle tier was not, which the manuscript records as a deviation.

Averaged over all series the best zero-shot configuration reaches 0.080 VUS-PR against 0.322 for a k-nearest-neighbour detector left at its defaults. Cost does not explain the gap and inverts it: once weights are resident the fastest foundation model beats the strongest baseline's throughput by 1.78×. Within a series, lower forecast error goes with better detection (rank correlation −0.415), contradicting the published explanation that these models fail by reconstructing anomalies too faithfully. A score-level moving average, using no labels and no extra inference, lifts them from 25 % to between 45 and 53 % of the best classical detector while leaving that detector unmoved. The bottleneck is the conversion from forecast to anomaly score, not the forecast.

A fourth result is methodological: of the four metrics used, one assigns a near-perfect score to detectors that flag everything, flag nothing, or predict in the wrong place. killtest/test_metrics.py is the adversarial audit that caught it, and it needs no data to run.

Version 1.1.0 adds the two controls the manuscript leans on, both released so they can be rerun rather than taken on trust. killtest/vus_reference_check.py compares our VUS-PR against the reference implementation of Paparrizos et al. on 1368 paired values (Spearman 0.991; the headline ratio moves from 34.0 % to 34.1 %). killtest/horizon_check.py measures the period-64 ramp that non-overlapping forecast blocks inject into every foundation-model score and shows it accounts for 2 % of what the score-level moving average recovers.

This record archives the code, the 5504 merged result records, the isolated cost profile and the five figures. The persisted anomaly scores (5504 arrays, 245 MB) are deposited as a separate dataset record. The four benchmark corpora are not redistributed; they carry their own licences and are versioned by their own maintainers. The manuscript is not included.
